fixes.explanation: Hold on, friend, that one's flipped. Paul says the opposite: "no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, 'Jesus be cursed…'" Somebody speaking by the Spirit just doesn't talk that way. That card got flipped faster than a cookie off the spatula.

That's right, baker. Paul says "no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, 'Jesus be cursed…'" So the claim on the card has it backwards. Someone speaking by the Spirit doesn't say that about Jesus.

Yes, baker. Paul says "…no one can say, 'Jesus is Lord,' except by the Holy Spirit." So those words come with the Spirit's help. And notice who Paul names in the next few verses: Spirit, Lord, God, all in a row.

Nice try, baker, but I checked this verse for a wing or a halo and came up empty. Paul says "…no one can say, 'Jesus is Lord,' except by the Holy Spirit." The credit goes to the Spirit, and Paul doesn't hand any of it to angels.

The church does show up later, baker. Paul says God appointed people in the church (1 Corinthians 12:28). But in this line it's "…the same God…" who works all things in all people. Paul puts the working on God.

That's it, baker. Paul says the manifestation of the Spirit is given to each one "…for the common good." So a gift isn't a trophy for the shelf. It's given for everyone's good, like a warm batch set out for the whole office.

True, baker. Paul says "…in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free…" Those he's talking about, Jews or Greeks, slave or free, were all baptized into the one body. Different backgrounds, one body.

Paul goes the other direction, friend. If the whole body were an eye, he asks, "…where would the sense of hearing be?" He's showing what's lost when there's only one kind of part. Later he adds, "The eye cannot say to the hand, 'I do not need you.'" (1 Corinthians 12:21).

Copying the eye would leave the body short, baker. Paul asks where hearing would be if the whole body were an eye, and where smell would be if it were an ear. He also asks, "If they were all one part, where would the body be?" (1 Corinthians 12:19). The picture is about different parts, not matching ones.

That's the word, baker. Paul says, "The eye cannot say to the hand, 'I do not need you.' Nor can the head say to the feet, 'I do not need you.'" No part gets to look at another part and say it can do without it.

Easy to mix up, friend, but this one is about need. Paul says, "The eye cannot say to the hand, 'I do not need you.'" The head can't say it to the feet either. I'd like to see a head try to get to work without them.
Waiting would be a funny reaction, friend. Paul says "if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it." Rejoices, not checks its watch. Picture a foot tapping while the hand gets the applause.
